title: International WASH & climate-resilience grants — next intake / waitlist
status: 2026 deadline passed; applications after June 30 placed on waitlist
geography: Selected countries across Africa, Asia and Latin America
eligible: Potentially — nonprofit eligibility plus new-partner reference requirement
reason: Canadian foundation with an explicit Water and Sanitation action area, grants up to $35,000, and a country list that overlaps heavily with WaterAid. The 2026 normal deadline has passed, so the best action is to prepare for the next cycle or ask about the waitlist.
next_action: Map a small, locally led WASH project to Roncalli criteria; verify next intake timing and identify a reference organization if WaterAid is treated as a new partner.
evidence: Roncalli funds 100+ Global South projects yearly; Water and Sanitation is an explicit action area; grants may be up to CAD 35,000; 2026 applications after June 30 go to a waitlist.

evidence_items.quote: Applications received after June 30, 2026 will be placed on a waiting list; projects must meet criteria and take place in a country where the Foundation works.
Water and Sanitation projects may include wells, pumps, reservoirs, latrines, handwashing stations, awareness and training.

title: International Development — maternal & child health / women & girls
status: 2026 EOI window closed; monitor next cycle
amount: Recent grants roughly CAD 20,000–250,000; varies by cycle
eligible: Registered Canadian charities can be eligible; verify next call
reason: The Foundation explicitly funds international development, has supported WASH-related work in Nigeria and Ethiopia, and its program guidance has linked WASH infrastructure to maternal and child health. The current 2026 EOI window is closed.
next_action: Add to Funding Watch and prepare a next-cycle case around WASH + maternal/child health or women and girls in a WaterAid priority country.
evidence: The International Development program supports women and girls, primarily in Sub-Saharan Africa; the 2026 EOI window closed July 13 and is under review.

evidence_items.quote: International Development focuses on Maternal & Child Health and Women & Girls Opportunity, with a primary focus on Sub-Saharan Africa; 2026 EOI window closed July 13.
Recent recipients include Lifewater Canada for clean water and sanitation in Nigeria and Operation Eyesight Canada for integrated WASH and maternal/child health in Ethiopia.

title: Unsolicited proposal pathway for international assistance
status: Applications accepted on an ongoing basis
eligible: Canadian NGOs and private-sector organizations may submit if requirements are met
reason: GAC is an established WaterAid Canada funder and accepts unsolicited proposals on an ongoing basis for ODA-eligible countries. This is strategically important but should be pursued only when a strong concept aligns with GAC priorities and WaterAid capacity.
next_action: Develop a concept around one or more WaterAid target countries and confirm fit against current GAC policy priorities before entering Partners@International.
evidence: GAC lists unsolicited proposals as ongoing for all ODA-eligible countries and non-governmental/private-sector organizations.

title: Canadian Climate Partnerships Initiative
eligible: No — only specifically invited organizations can apply; WaterAid Canada is not on the published invitee list
reason: Strong geographic and climate-resilience fit, but the call is invitation-only and WaterAid Canada is not among the published invitees. This is exactly the kind of attractive-looking opportunity the system should reject early.
next_action: Do not spend proposal hours on this call. Monitor future GAC climate-finance opportunities and partnership routes.
evidence: The call is invitation-only and publishes the invited organizations; WaterAid Canada is not listed.
